clue.text: Possibly a feature of fair skin, except when reflected

parts.note: bran is the husk or outer skin of cereal grain, sifted off when flour is milled

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, so the word for except is read backwards

parts.note: but means except, as in 'all but one'

explanation.surface: A beauty tip: fair skin looks a certain way, except in a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair skin' reads as a complexion, but 'fair' belongs to the definition and 'skin' is the first piece. A BRAN TUB is a lucky dip at a British fete: a tub of bran with prizes buried in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky-dip barrel of bran hiding small prizes is a typical stall at a village fete, so 'possibly' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Concise instructions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short and to the point
second meaning: a set of instructions, as given to a barrister or a mission team

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something short and a noun for the instructions a lawyer or agent is given.

clue.text: Removal of cars not a bit unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Taking cars off the road is no rare thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstraction is the act of taking something away or withdrawing it, as in abstracting water from a river.

clue.text: As Rossini opera might be described for singer?

definitions.text: As Rossini opera might be described
definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: Rossini's opera William Tell tells the story of Tell
second meaning: someone who sings to the police is an informer, one who tells tales

explanation.walkthrough: To 'sing' is slang for informing on someone, so a singer here is a sneak, not a vocalist, despite the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale is a person who reports others' misdeeds, a sneak or informer who blabs.

clue.text: Person helping polish big gun in building

parts.note: a brick is an old-fashioned word for a reliable, helpful person
to sand is to smooth and polish a surface
a mortar is a heavy artillery piece firing shells at high angles

explanation.surface: Someone helps clean a large cannon inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You're a brick' is dated British praise for a person who helps out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricks and mortar is an idiom for buildings or property, especially as an investment.

clue.text: On moving right to the left out in the open

indicators.note: moving signals that the letter for right shifts its place within the word for on
to the left says which way the right letter shifts: earlier in the word

parts.note: on board a ship or train is aboard, so 'on' gives this word

explanation.surface: Instructions for a dance or drill: shift right to left, out in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: In ABOARD the R moves one place left, ahead of the O, giving ABROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad has an old sense of outdoors or at large, widely about, as in 'ghosts walk abroad'.

clue.text: Canopy, wide but with no top

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: yawning means gaping wide open, as in a yawning gap

explanation.surface: Describing a canopy: broad, but with no roof over it.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a sheet of canvas stretched over a frame as a shelter, a kind of canopy.

clue.text: Oddly rhymes with 'Winchelsea' added to the original five

definitions.text: with 'Winchelsea' added to the original five

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what rhymes with the word Winchelsea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cinque Ports were five Kentish and Sussex harbour towns; Rye and Winchelsea were later added to them as the 'Ancient Towns'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is the Sussex port joined with Winchelsea to the original five Cinque Ports.

clue.text: Artificial ingredient contains carbon, causing dependency

indicators.note: contains means the word for the ingredient holds the carbon symbol inside it

parts.note: an additive is a substance added to food, often artificial
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A warning label: this food additive has carbon in it and is habit-forming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something addictive is habit-forming, creating a need for it.

clue.text: Oil peters out — last drops of the well

parts.note: to peter out is to fade away and stop, so it dies

indicators.note: the last drops of a word are its final letters, here of 'the' and 'well'

explanation.surface: An oil well running dry, down to its last drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is a heavy fuel oil distilled from petroleum and burnt in compression-ignition engines.

clue.text: Nude in no improper suggestion

indicators.note: improper means not in proper order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prudish ruling: no nudity, nor any risque suggestion either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improper' looks like part of the definition (an improper suggestion), but it is the anagram signal and the definition is just 'suggestion'.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect hint, usually a sly or smutty one, so it is a kind of suggestion.

clue.text: A group of fliers returning from a long way off

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters for the air force are read in the other direction

parts.note: the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force, is a body of pilots

explanation.surface: A squadron of pilots coming home from distant parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb for at a great distance, a literary word for far away.

clue.text: Disconcerted king held by methodical revolutionary, cryptically

indicators.note: held by means placed inside the word that holds it
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for methodical is read backwards

parts.note: neat means orderly, tidy and methodical
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
cryptically tells you to read the answer as a description of its own wordplay: the second word, split as 'a back', names the backwards reading just done

explanation.surface: A tidy-minded rebel is unsettled after taking a king hostage.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer describes itself: K taken into NEAT read a back way. Bloggers found it circular, since 'revolutionary' and 'aback' both signal the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken aback is an idiom for being startled or caught off guard, thrown off balance.

clue.text: Sadly, China's all but abandoning one large Asian region

indicators.note: sadly means in a sorry state, so these letters are jumbled
abandoning one means a single copy of the large letter is left out of the jumble

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A lament: China is all but giving up a big region of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' looks like 'almost', but both words are fodder; one of the two Ls in ALL is dropped before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Baluchistan is a vast mountainous area spanning western Pakistan, south-eastern Iran and part of Afghanistan.

clue.text: My fault — Paul came — out of order

indicators.note: out of order means not in sequence, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone apologises: Paul arrived when he should not have, and it is my fault.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase from the Confiteor is an admission of guilt, used in English to own up to an error.

clue.text: Meet in Parisian bar

parts.note: en is French for in, so a Parisian's 'in'
a counter is the bar across which drinks are served

explanation.surface: An arrangement to meet in a bar in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' takes the word 'in' with it: EN is French for in.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone is to come across or come face to face with them.

clue.text: Little animal in reality starts here?

definitions.text: Little animal in reality starts here?

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, taken from the four words before it

explanation.surface: A wondering question: does a small creature's real life begin here?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the opening letters spell the word, and a young animal does begin life in its den.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild animal's den or resting place, where young are born and raised.

clue.text: I heard you are beset by a sort of milder hysteria

indicators.note: are beset by means surrounded, so the I and U go inside the jumbled word
a sort of means a sorting or rearrangement of the next word's letters
heard means spoken aloud, so you becomes the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are suffering a mild form of hysteria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you are' looks like it should sound like UR, but only 'you' is heard; 'are beset by' puts IU inside DELRM, the rearranged MILDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium is a state of wild excitement and frenzy, used loosely as uncontrolled emotional excitement.

clue.text: Type of berry found over in Victoria, Canada

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters found are read backwards
in means the letters are sitting within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A traveller reports spotting a kind of berry in Victoria, British Columbia.
explanation.definitionFit: The acai is a small purple palm fruit from South America, marketed as a superfood.

clue.text: Soaked headless fish in a bit of dessert wine

indicators.note: a bit of a word is here its first letter, of dessert

parts.note: first letter of dessert

indicators.note: in means the shortened fish sits inside the word for wine

parts.note: red is a common shorthand for red wine

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the fish is removed

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A dinner where a fish course gets drowned in sweet wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Drenched means wet through, thoroughly saturated, the same as soaked.

clue.text: Are clutching a CD excitedly, for playing here?

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the word are wraps round the jumbled letters
excitedly means in a stirred-up way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly holding a compact disc, ready to play it.
explanation.walkthrough: The CD in the surface suggests music, but the playing is on games machines.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a hall of slot machines and video games, a place to play.

clue.text: Michelangelo's Apollo: ultimately limited, lacking finish, but I will acquire it

indicators.note: will acquire means the first pair of words takes in the rest inside it
ultimately means at the end, so take the final letter of Apollo

parts.note: last letter of Apollo

indicators.note: lacking finish means the word's last letter is dropped

parts.note: narrow means limited, restricted

explanation.surface: An art critic's verdict on Michelangelo's Apollo statue, which was left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: Michelangelo's Apollo really is unfinished, which makes 'lacking finish' fit the surface. Buonarroti was his family surname, so 'Michelangelo's' means his other name.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni was the artist's full name, so his surname is the possessive's object.

clue.text: Bird heading off reaches Scottish island

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the bird is taken away

parts.note: the finch is a small seed-eating songbird

explanation.surface: A bird flies off and arrives at a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: An inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm in the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots and Gaelic place names an inch is an islet, often in a river or loch.

clue.text: Hidden store of money, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is reported or said, so the word sounds like the money word

parts.note: cash is money in notes and coins

explanation.surface: Rumours of a secret stash of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a concealed hoard of goods, weapons or valuables kept in a secret place.

clue.text: Children's game with Grandma in street, standing still

indicators.note: in means the game and grandma go inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: tag is a chasing game played by children
nan is a British pet name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: Kids play a game with their grandmother out in the road, not moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant describes water or air that is motionless and not flowing, hence stale.

clue.text: Animal sung about endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off
about means turned round, so the word sung is read backwards

explanation.surface: A creature that has been the subject of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Flanders and Swann sang 'The Gnu Song', which makes the surface true.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu, or wildebeest, is a large African antelope with a beard and curved horns.

clue.text: In time, performance will be perfect

parts.note: an act is a turn or performance on stage

explanation.surface: Given time, the show will be flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means whole and undamaged, so perfect in the sense of complete and unblemished.

clue.text: A river and its name evoke a reaction

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
the Ouse is the name of several English rivers, so it names the river

explanation.surface: A river and what it is called stir up some feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse is to stir up or awaken a feeling or response in someone, provoking it.

clue.text: Italian church affair

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian from Rome
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Italian church scandal: someone is having an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair, a relationship of passion.
